institution.name: The University of Texas at El Paso

plan.notes: Source: official UTEP 2026-2027 Undergraduate Catalog, BS in Computer Science (Department of Computer Science, College of Engineering), retrieved 2026-09-30 from https://catalog.utep.edu/undergrad/college-of-engineering/computer-science/computer-science-bs/ and its official program PDF (computer-science-bs.pdf, generated by the catalog 2026-06-04). Transcription method: manual transcription of the catalog's official 4-Year Sample Degree Plan 'BS in Computer Science (Starting with Calculus)' (8 semesters, Fall/Spring, no concentration). Catalog-year basis: catalog.utep.edu homepage titles the current catalog '2026-2027 Catalog'. CREDIT CAVEAT: the degree requires 120 credits, but UTEP's own published 'Starting with Calculus' sample sequence totals 119 (its PDF prints 'Total Hours: 119'). total_credits is therefore 119, the true sum of the transcribed sample plan, not 120; a student following this sample would need one additional elective credit to reach 120. Titles follow the catalog's sample-plan wording verbatim. Choice slots (choice:true) mirror the catalog's '*' core-curriculum placeholders and named slots (Technical Elective, Free Elective, Additional Math or Science Lecture, Life and Physical Science Lecture and Lab); each choice_note cites the catalog's selection rules. The 'Starting with Pre-Calculus' track (adds MATH 1508/MATH 1310 in a summer term, 122-124 hours) and the three concentrations (Secure Cyber Systems, Software Engineering, Data Analytics) are NOT encoded; this is the base degree plan. Prerequisites: encoded only from the official UTEP catalog CS course descriptions (catalog.utep.edu/undergrad/course-descriptions/cs/), using the pathway satisfiable by in-plan courses. Many upper-division CS courses also accept MATH 2300 (Discrete Mathematics) as an alternative to CS 2202; the degree plan offers 'MATH 2300 OR CS 2101 + CS 2202' and this sample sequence takes CS 2101 + CS 2202, so prereqs are encoded via the CS 2202 pathway. Catalog prereqs carry grade-C-or-better conditions and some require departmental approval (e.g., CS 4310) — details live in the official course descriptions; consult the catalog and an advisor. All designated-core and core-curriculum courses require a grade of C or better per the catalog.

courses.title: Additional Math or Science Lecture — student choice
courses.choice_note: Additional Mathematics or Science Option (3 cr) — student choice. Option A: one math course (e.g., MATH 2313, MATH 2325, MATH 2326, MATH 3320, MATH 3325, MATH 4329, STAT 4380, STAT 4385). Option B: an additional 3-credit lecture course from the Life and Physical Science list that was NOT used to satisfy the science lecture/lab requirement (official catalog note).

courses.title: Life and Physical Science Lecture and Lab — student choice
courses.choice_note: One semester of lecture and associated lab (4 cr) — student choice. Per the official catalog note, in addition to PHYS 2320, acceptable pairs include: ASTR 1307 + ASTR 1107; PHYS 2421; BIOL 1305 + BIOL 1107; BIOL 1306 + BIOL 1108; CHEM 1305 + CHEM 1105; CHEM 1306 + CHEM 1106; GEOL 1313 + GEOL 1103; GEOL 1314 + GEOL 1104. Requires grade C or better.

No more than 3 credit hours of CS 1xxx/2xxx, and no more than 6 credit hours of CS 1xxx/2xxx, CS 4181, CS 4371, CS 4x73, CS 4392, CS 4393 (any combination) may count (official catalog note).
